title: Veyra Bot Metadata Manifest
description: JSON Schema for the veyra.json manifest required for submissions to the Veyra bot catalog. It implements version 1.0 of the Veyra Bot Metadata Specification.
$comment: Duplicate variable names, SPDX License List membership, catalog license policy, and credential scanning are enforced by the Veyra submission system because JSON Schema cannot express those checks.

schemaVersion.description: Version of the manifest format. For schema version 1.0 the only accepted value is the string "1.0".

name.description: Public bot name shown in the catalog. Between 2 and 60 ASCII characters; the first character must be a letter or digit, the last character must be a letter, digit, dot, underscore, or hyphen, and internal spaces are allowed.

description.description: Short public description used on catalog cards and detail pages. Between 10 and 280 characters and must not start or end with whitespace.
examples: A small example bot used in the documentation.

category.description: Controlled catalog category. Arbitrary values are not accepted; see the category table in the specification.

version.description: Bot release version in Semantic Versioning 2.0.0 format. Pre-release and build metadata are accepted.

license.description: SPDX license identifier or a simple SPDX expression using AND, OR, or WITH. Parentheses are not supported in schema version 1.0. Use LicenseRef-Proprietary for proprietary projects; such projects are not open source and are not eligible for the public catalog.

repository.description: Public source code repository URL. Only HTTPS URLs are accepted.

runtime.description: Runtime information used for catalog filters and compatibility checks.

language.description: Primary implementation language in lowercase canonical form. Any language is allowed; VBS permits language-agnostic bots. Examples: typescript, javascript, python, java, csharp, go, rust, ruby, php.

version.description: Minimum supported runtime version, expressed as one to three numeric components separated by dots (for example 24, 24.0, 24.0.0, or 3.12).

requirements.description: Additional runtime requirements, such as external services, native packages, or Docker. Omit the property or use an empty array when there are none.

items.description: A single runtime requirement. Must not start or end with whitespace.

variables.description: Environment variables the bot reads. The array may be empty. Variable names must be unique; JSON Schema cannot enforce uniqueness of a property across array items, so the Veyra submission system performs that semantic check.

name.description: Environment variable name. Uppercase ASCII letters, digits, and underscores; it must start with a letter and be unique within the array.

description.description: Purpose of the variable and the accepted values. Must not start or end with whitespace.
examples: Token used to authenticate the bot with Discord.

required.description: When true, Veyra must collect a value before generating a distribution package. A required variable cannot define a default.

secret.description: When true, the value is sensitive: Veyra must mask it, never log or display it, and never store it in plaintext in the catalog. A secret variable cannot define a default.

default.description: Optional default value applied when an optional, non-secret variable is left empty. The manifest is public, so defaults must never contain credentials. Forbidden when required or secret is true.

examples.name: Example Bot
examples.description: A small example bot used in the documentation.
